title: Analytical Solutions of the Generalized Klein-Gordon Oscillator in Som-Raychaudhuri Space-Time via the Extended Nikiforov-Uvarov Method
authors: Hale Karayer, Tolga Celik, Dogan Demirhan
abstract: In this study, we present an analytical approach based on the extended Nikiforov-Uvarov method to solve the generalized Klein-Gordon oscillator in the presence of a uniform magnetic field within the Som-Raychaudhuri space-time. Exact eigenstate solutions are obtained for two distinct potential models, namely the linear potential and the Cornell potential. The corresponding energy eigenvalues are determined, and the associated eigenfunctions are analyzed and illustrated graphically.
summary: This paper analytically solves the generalized Klein-Gordon oscillator equation in the Som-Raychaudhuri space-time using the extended Nikiforov-Uvarov method. It derives explicit energy spectra and eigenfunctions for linear and Cornell potentials, showing how topological defects and magnetic fields influence the quantum energy levels. The work provides a systematic algebraic framework for solving relativistic quantum problems in curved backgrounds.
main_problem: The study aims to find exact analytical solutions for the generalized Klein-Gordon oscillator equation within the curved Som-Raychaudhuri space-time.
main_result: Analytical solutions for the energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions are obtained for both linear and Cornell potential models, expressed in terms of biconfluent Heun polynomials.
method: The research employs the extended Nikiforov-Uvarov (NU) method, a powerful analytical technique used to solve the resulting radial differential equations.
model_or_system: The system models a relativistic quantum particle governed by the Klein-Gordon equation, incorporating effects from a uniform magnetic field and an oscillator potential in the Som-Raychaudhuri space-time.
important_parameters: Topological parameter ($\alpha$), magnetic field strength ($B_0$), oscillator frequency ($\omega$), and particle mass ($M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the solvability of the radial equation using the extended NU formalism and restricts the analysis to specific potential forms (linear and Cornell).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the radial wave functions ($\psi(r)$) for different quantum numbers and potential types, while tables present calculated positive energy eigenvalues.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the KG oscillator in this space-time, introduces the extended NU method, derives solutions for the linear and Cornell potentials, and concludes by discussing the physical implications of the derived spectra.
why_interesting: While focused on curved spacetime QFT, the use of advanced analytical techniques like the extended NU method to solve complex differential equations is a valuable theoretical tool applicable to other non-standard quantum Hamiltonians.
